headline: Warren Buffett, 96, steps down as Berkshire chairman
summary: Buffett has chaired Berkshire Hathaway since 1970. On Friday he became chairman emeritus and handed the job to his son Howard, a board member since 1993. Greg Abel took over as CEO at the start of this year. Buffett wrote to shareholders: "Greg runs the company; Howard will guard its culture and values."

cover_question.q: Why did he quit if he liked it?

cover_answer: He's 96. He stays on the board, and his son takes over.
table_question: Should the boss's kid get the boss's job?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A famous money man named Warren Buffett is 96 years old. On Friday he gave the top job at his company to his son Howard. It's like a coach who stops calling the plays but still sits on the bench. He says he has never felt better about what comes next.
5-7.why: A coach moving to the bench is a handoff they've seen. Nobody is in trouble.

8-12.script: Warren Buffett turned an old textile company into Berkshire Hathaway, worth a trillion dollars. He handed it off in steps: Greg Abel became CEO in January, and now his son Howard is chairman. Like a coach and a captain.
8-12.why: Coach and captain make the CEO-versus-chairman split make sense.

13-17.script: Should a founder's son get the chairman's job? Buffett calls Howard "a policy the shareholders own and hope never to claim against." Berkshire has beaten the market since 1965 but lagged it over the last decade. Is a family name a safeguard or a shortcut?
13-17.why: Teens have opinions about inherited advantages. Let them argue it first.

5-7.q: Why did he quit if he liked it?
5-7.a: He's 96, and he didn't quit all the way. He stays on the board, and his son and a man named Greg run things now.

8-12.a: The articles don't say. He has given away about $66 billion of stock since 2006, so a lot.
Leads the board. Greg Abel is the CEO and runs the company day to day. Howard will guard its culture, Buffett says.

13-17.q: Should a founder's son get the chairman's job?
13-17.a: Howard has been on the board since 1993, and Buffett planned this for years. A professor says the test is whether Abel and Howard can adapt.
Yes. As CEO he nearly doubled the S&P 500's return, 19.9% a year to 10.4%. The last decade was closer to even.
